prerequisites: Previous participation in the "Physics" module is desirable.

learning_outcomes.text: After successful completion of the module, students can explain the function, structure, and applications of sensors in mechanical engineering.
They can interpret and critically evaluate sensor-generated measurement data.
Depending on the task and application area, students can select suitable sensors.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to critically evaluate the significance of measurement results.

syllabus_topics: Mechanoresistive sensors e.g. strain gauges for force or torque measurements
Capacitive sensors e.g. position sensors, level sensors
Magneto-inductive sensors e.g. displacement sensors or gear speed sensors based on a Hall element, Fluxgate magnetometer for non-destructive material testing
Interferometric sensors e.g. for thin film thickness determination
Time-of-flight based sensors e.g. ultrasonic sensors for material testing
Doppler-effect based sensors e.g. flow sensors
Other sensors e.g. flow sensors, temperature sensors etc.
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded for a passed written exam. The significance of the grade for the final grade is determined by the Bachelor's examination regulations.
